subject: Post-call: inference enclave fit & ops priorities
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@stratify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: inference enclave fit & ops priorities

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap so we have a shared artifact and clear next steps.

High-level goal you described:
- Move StratifyAI from a cluster-based hybrid inference approach to a dedicated, predictable inference fabric for customer-facing features (chat + recommendations). Primary objective is 99th percentile latency under 200ms for 512-token requests at peak.

Key pain points you confirmed:
1) Noisy multi-tenant variability — spikes from experiments knock downstream SLAs.
2) Cost unpredictability — bursty inference from batch jobs causes large monthly swings.
3) Compliance/data isolation for PII-heavy workloads in EU customers.

What we heard about requirements:
- Committed pool with tenant isolation (per-customer VLAN + KMS integration)
- Burst capacity to cover 2.5x peak for campaign windows
- Ops SLOs: 99.9% availability for the committed pool; 99th latency target 200ms for production endpoints
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, end-to-end trace sampling for tail latency analysis

Preliminary sizing you gave on call:
- 30M monthly inference tokens initially; estimated peak concurrency ~180 qps for 512-token median calls (higher during campaigns)

Attachments I'm including for reference:
- Stratify_MVP_traffic.xlsx (your traffic sketch you dropped in the meeting)
- SLA-draft-stratify.pdf (initial SLA template we discussed)

Immediate next steps we recommend (to confirm by EOD Mon):
1) You: confirm whether EU customer set requires on-prem or VPC-private deployment vs hosted Dedicated in our eu-west region.
2) Us (Monica/Ben): provide committed-pool sizing options (3 configs) + pricing delta for isolation + burst policy options.
3) Ben/Jordan: draft a sample mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for procurement and pilot.

If the above aligns, we'll prepare a short options matrix (S, M, L pool) with expected throughput, cost, and SLA handoffs.

Thanks —
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the crisp recap, that matches our view. A couple clarifications / extra context: 

- EU requirement: for now we need VPC-private (we cannot go on shared-hosted eu region for the set of customers in scope). Not on-prem yet, but want keys in our KMS and audit log export to our Splunk instance.
- Peak concurrency: the 180 qps was for conversational workloads; recommendations endpoints are lighter (median 80 qps) but have heavy burst windows during prep.
- Campaigns: expect 36–48 hour periodic spikes 2–3x sustained; burst capacity is critical.
- Budget: upper bound for committed capacity year 1 is ~$450k — we can trade on SLA/tail latency commitments.

We reviewed the SLA-draft and left a few inline comments (I'll upload a marked copy next week). For now, please prioritize: (1) isolation & KMS flow for VPC deployment, (2) a small pilot plan (6–8 weeks) that proves tail latency under load, (3) pricing tiers that show committed vs burst economics.

Appreciate it —
Alex
CTO, StratifyAI
alex.jensen@stratify.ai

Can you please:

Team — quick commercial/ops note after reviewing the sketch and the numbers Alex gave. Summary of the options I'll produce (target delivery Tue EOD):

1) Option S (pilot-focused)
   - Committed pool: 8 A100-equivalent slots (quantized runtime)
   - Sustained throughput: ~90 qps for 512-token median, burst to 270 qps (3x) via pre-warmed spare capacity
   - SLA: 99.5% availability for pilot pool; 99th latency ~260ms at pilot load (we'll tune inference kernels during the pilot)
   - Year-1 committed price: $160k (includes 8-week pilot run & 25% integration efforts)

2) Option M (production baseline)
   - Committed pool: 24 A100-equivalent slots
   - Sustained throughput: ~280 qps for 512-token median, burst to 700 qps (2.5x)
   - SLA: 99.9% availability; 99th latency target 200ms with optimized kernels + KV cache warmers
   - Year-1 committed price: $420k (includes VPC-private setup, KMS integration, and 3 months of priority support)

3) Option L (enterprise stance)
   - Committed pool: 48 slots, redundant multi-az placement
   - Sustained throughput: ~560 qps, burst to 1400 qps
   - SLA: 99.95% availability; 99th latency target 150–180ms with dedicated ops runbook
   - Year-1 committed price: $760k (includes multi-az, dedicated SRE allocation, and expanded retention/trace sampling)

Commercial notes / caveats:
- VPC-private isolation + KMS has a one-time integration fee (we'll line-item; ballpark $25k) and modest monthly footprint (~5% premium).
- Pilot acceptance criteria should include a reproducible load profile and an agreed dataset that approximates tail behavior. If they cannot provide that, we will run a synthetic profile but will discount the pilot guarantees.
- We should include a fallback policy: if we miss latency SLOs post-rollout, automatic failover to a broader fleet and credits per the SLA draft.

Monica — if this looks reasonable I'll assemble the pricing attachment and a one-page MAP for Jordan to slot milestones into. Jordan — flag any additional operational gates you want included.

Ben
